items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: That was sort of a rite of passage for the Pizzarellis. Because Mary had learned it previously when she was fifteen.

ctx.x: Yeah. And so there were the chords, now see? And it works with the records. So I’d play along with records. And gravitated toward learning Peter Frampton solos and all that, that went along with that. I mean my father had amps and guitars, so I was the guy. “Come on over, we’ve got the equipment.” Plugging everything into one amplifier, the whole band came out. And so along the way my father said, “Well okay” actually he tells it, which is strange, is that there was a trombone player a couple of towns over who…
McDonough duet and I played the second part. That was sort of a rite of passage for the Pizzarellis. Because Mary had learned it previously when she was fifteen. A very hip family.
